verses.16:28: Then the one who burns them shall wash his garments and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he may enter the camp.
verses.16:29: And this shall be a perpetual statute for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month, you shall afflict your souls and shall not do any work, neither the native nor the resident alien who resides among you.
verses.16:30: For on this day atonement shall be made for you to cleanse you; from all your sins you shall be clean before the LORD.
verses.16:31: It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall afflict your souls; it is a perpetual statute.
verses.16:32: And the priest who is anointed and ordained to serve as priest in place of his father shall make atonement, and he shall put on the linen garments, the holy garments.
verses.16:33: He shall make atonement for the holy sanctuary, and he shall make atonement for the tent of meeting and for the altar; he shall also make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
verses.16:34: And this shall be a perpetual statute for you, to make atonement for the sons of Israel for all their sins once a year." And he did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.17:1: Now the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.17:2: "Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to all the sons of Israel, and tell them, 'This is the word that the LORD has commanded, saying,
verses.17:3: "Any man from the house of Israel who slaughters an ox or a lamb or a goat inside the camp, or who slaughters outside the camp,
verses.17:4: and has not brought it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to present an offering to the LORD before the tabernacle of the LORD, blood shall be charged to that man; he has shed blood, and that man shall be cut off from the midst of his people;
verses.17:5: in order that the sons of Israel may bring their sacrifices that they are sacrificing in the open field, and bring them to the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, to the priest, and sacrifice them as sacrifices of peace offerings to the LORD.
verses.17:6: And the priest shall splash the blood on the altar of the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and offer up the fat in smoke for a soothing fragrance to the LORD.
verses.17:7: And they shall no longer sacrifice their sacrifices to the goat-demons after whom they are prostituting themselves. This shall be a perpetual statute for them throughout their generations."'
verses.17:8: And to them you shall say, 'Any man from the house of Israel, or from the resident aliens who reside in their midst, who offers up a burnt offering or a sacrifice,
verses.17:9: and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to prepare it for the LORD, then that man shall be cut off from his kinspeople.
verses.17:10: And as for any man from the house of Israel, or from the resident aliens who reside in their midst, who eats any blood, I will set My face against the person who eats the blood, and I will cut him off from the midst of his people.
verses.17:11: For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I Myself have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives; for it is the blood that makes atonement by means of the life.
verses.17:12: Therefore I have said to the sons of Israel, "No person among you shall eat blood, and the resident alien who resides in your midst shall not eat blood."
verses.17:13: And any man from the sons of Israel, or from the resident aliens who reside in their midst, who hunts game, a wild animal or a bird that may be eaten, shall pour out its blood and cover it with dust.
verses.17:14: For as to the life of all flesh, its blood is one with its life; so I said to the sons of Israel, "You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood; everyone who eats it shall be cut off."
verses.17:15: And every person who eats what died naturally or what was torn, whether native-born or a resident alien, shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until the evening; then he shall be clean.
verses.17:16: But if he does not wash them and does not bathe his flesh, then he shall bear his iniquity.'"
verses.18:1: Now the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.18:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and tell them, 'I am the LORD your God.
verses.18:3: You must not do according to the practice of the land of Egypt, where you lived, and you must not do according to the practice of the land of Canaan, into which I am bringing you; and you must not walk in their statutes.
verses.18:4: My ordinances you shall do, and My statutes you shall keep, to walk in them; I am the LORD your God.
verses.18:5: And you shall keep My statutes and My ordinances; a person who does them will live by them. I am the LORD.
verses.18:6: No man among you shall approach any close kin of his flesh to uncover nakedness; I am the LORD.
verses.18:7: You must not uncover the nakedness of your father and the nakedness of your mother; she is your mother; you must not uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:8: You must not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife; it is the nakedness of your father.
verses.18:9: As for the nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother, whether born at home or born outside, you must not uncover their nakedness.
verses.18:10: As for the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, you must not uncover their nakedness, for they are your nakedness.
verses.18:11: As for the nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife, born to your father—she is your sister—you must not uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:12: You must not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister; she is your father's close kin.
verses.18:13: You must not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, for she is your mother's close kin.
verses.18:14: You must not uncover the nakedness of your father's brother; you must not approach his wife; she is your aunt.
verses.18:15: You must not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law; she is your son's wife; you must not uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:16: You must not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife; it is the nakedness of your brother.
verses.18:17: You must not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter; you must not take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to uncover her nakedness; they are close kin; it is depravity.
verses.18:18: And you must not take a woman in addition to her sister as a rival, to uncover her nakedness alongside her during her lifetime.
verses.18:19: And you must not approach a woman during her menstrual uncleanness to uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:20: And with your neighbor's wife you must not lie sexually, to become defiled by her.
verses.18:21: And you must not give any of your seed to make them pass over to Molech, and you must not profane the name of your God; I am the LORD.
verses.18:22: And with a male you must not lie as one lies with a woman; it is an abomination.
verses.18:23: And with any animal you must not lie sexually, to become defiled by it; and a woman must not stand before an animal for it to mate with her; it is perversion.
verses.18:24: Do not defile yourselves by any of these things, for by all these things the nations whom I am expelling from before you have become defiled.
verses.18:25: And the land became defiled, so I visited its iniquity upon it, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
verses.18:26: But you yourselves shall keep My statutes and My ordinances, and you must not commit any of these abominations, neither the native-born nor the resident alien who resides in your midst—
verses.18:27: for the men of the land who were before you committed all these abominations, and the land became defiled—
verses.18:28: so that the land will not vomit you out when you defile it, just as it vomited out the nation that was before you.
verses.18:29: For anyone who commits any of these abominations, the persons who commit them shall be cut off from the midst of their people.
verses.18:30: Therefore you shall keep My charge, so as not to practice any of the abominable statutes that were practiced before you, and you must not defile yourselves by them; I am the LORD your God.'"
verses.19:1: Now the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.19:2: "Speak to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel and say to them, 'You are to be holy, because I, the LORD your God, am holy.
verses.19:3: Each of you must revere his mother and his father, and you must observe My Sabbaths; I am the LORD your God.
verses.19:4: Do not turn toward idols, and do not make cast-metal gods for yourselves; I am the LORD your God.
verses.19:5: When you offer a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD, you must sacrifice it so that it will be accepted on your behalf.
verses.19:6: It is to be eaten on the day of your sacrifice and on the following day, and whatever remains until the third day shall be burned in fire.
verses.19:7: And if it is indeed eaten on the third day, it is a foul thing; it will not be accepted.
verses.19:8: Whoever eats it will bear his iniquity, because he has profaned the LORD's holy thing, and that person shall be cut off from his people.
verses.19:9: And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish reaping to the edge of your field, nor gather the gleanings of your harvest.
verses.19:10: And you shall not glean your vineyard, nor gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and for the resident alien. I am the LORD your God.
verses.19:11: You shall not steal; you shall not deceive, and you shall not lie, anyone to his fellow countryman.
verses.19:12: And you shall not swear in My name to a falsehood, and thus profane the name of your God; I am the LORD.
verses.19:13: You must not oppress your neighbor or rob him; the wages of a hired laborer must not stay overnight with you until morning.
verses.19:14: You shall not curse a deaf person, nor set a stumbling block before a blind person; rather, you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.
verses.19:15: You shall not commit injustice in judgment: you shall not favor a poor man, nor show deference to a great man; in righteousness you shall judge your fellow countryman.
verses.19:16: You shall not walk about as a slanderer among your people; you shall not stand against the blood of your neighbor. I am the LORD.
verses.19:17: You shall not hate your brother in your heart; you shall surely rebuke your fellow countryman, and not bear sin on account of him.
verses.19:18: You shall not take vengeance, nor hold a grudge against the sons of your people; instead, you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
verses.19:19: You shall observe My statutes: you shall not breed two kinds of your livestock together, you shall not sow your field with two kinds of seed, and a garment of two kinds of mixed weave shall not come upon you.
verses.19:20: Now if a man lies with a woman in sexual relations, and she is a slave woman designated for another man, yet she has not at all been redeemed nor has freedom been granted to her, there shall be an inquiry; they shall not be put to death, because she had not been freed.
verses.19:21: He shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, a ram as a guilt offering.
verses.19:22: Then the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the LORD on account of his sin that he has committed, and he will be forgiven for his sin that he has committed.
verses.19:23: And when you enter the land and plant any kind of food tree, you shall count its fruit as uncircumcised; for three years it shall be uncircumcised for you; it shall not be eaten.
verses.19:24: And in the fourth year, all its fruit shall be holy, for praise to the LORD.
verses.19:25: Then in the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so as to increase its yield for you. I am the LORD your God.
verses.19:26: You must not eat anything with the blood; you must not practice divination, nor engage in fortune-telling.
verses.19:27: You shall not round off the edges of your head, nor disfigure the edge of your beard.
verses.19:28: You shall not make any gash in your flesh for the dead, nor place any tattoo mark on yourselves; I am the LORD.
verses.19:29: Do not profane your daughter by causing her to engage in prostitution, so that the land will not turn to prostitution and the land become filled with depravity.
verses.19:30: You must observe My Sabbaths and revere My sanctuary; I am the LORD.
verses.19:31: Do not turn toward mediums or toward spirit-diviners; do not seek to become defiled by them. I am the LORD your God.
verses.19:32: Before one with gray hair you shall rise, and you shall honor the presence of an old man, and you shall fear your God; I am the LORD.
verses.19:33: And when a resident alien lives with you in your land, you shall not mistreat him.
verses.19:34: The resident alien who lives with you shall be to you like a native from among you, and you shall love him as yourself, because you were resident aliens in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
verses.19:35: You shall not commit injustice in judgment: in measurement of length, in weight, or in capacity.
verses.19:36: You shall have honest scales, honest weights, an honest ephah, and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt.
verses.19:37: Therefore you shall observe all My statutes and all My judgments, and carry them out; I am the LORD.'"
verses.20:1: Now the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.20:2: "And to the sons of Israel you shall say, 'Anyone from the sons of Israel, or from the resident aliens who live in Israel, who gives any of his seed to Molech shall surely be put to death; the people of the land shall stone him with stones.
verses.20:3: And I Myself will set My face against that man and cut him off from the midst of his people, because he gave some of his seed to Molech, so as to defile My sanctuary and to profane My holy name.
verses.20:4: And if the people of the land ever hide their eyes from that man when he gives some of his seed to Molech, so as not to put him to death,
verses.20:5: then I Myself will set My face against that man and against his family, and I will cut off him and all who prostitute themselves after him, prostituting themselves after Molech, from the midst of their people.
verses.20:6: As for the person who turns toward mediums and toward spirit-diviners to prostitute himself after them, I will set My face against that person and cut him off from the midst of his people.
verses.20:7: Therefore sanctify yourselves and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.
verses.20:8: And you shall observe My statutes and carry them out; I am the LORD who sanctifies you.
verses.20:9: Indeed, anyone who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death; he has cursed his father or his mother; his bloodguilt is on him.
verses.20:10: Now if a man commits adultery with another man's wife, one who commits adultery with the wife of his neighbor, the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.
verses.20:11: And if a man lies with his father's wife, he has uncovered the nakedness of his father; the two of them shall surely be put to death; their bloodguilt is on them.
verses.20:12: And if a man lies with his daughter-in-law, the two of them shall surely be put to death; they have committed a perversion; their bloodguilt is on them.
verses.20:13: And if a man lies with a male as one lies with a woman, the two of them have committed an abomination; they shall surely be put to death; their bloodguilt is on them.
verses.20:14: And if a man takes a woman and her mother, it is depravity; they shall burn him and them in fire, so that there will be no depravity in your midst.
verses.20:15: And if a man has sexual relations with an animal, he shall surely be put to death, and you shall kill the animal.
verses.20:16: And if a woman approaches any animal to mate with it, you must kill the woman and the animal; they shall surely be put to death; their bloodguilt is on them.
verses.20:17: And if a man takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness while she sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace, and they shall be cut off before the eyes of the sons of their people; he has uncovered the nakedness of his sister, and he shall bear his iniquity.
verses.20:18: And if a man lies with a menstruating woman and uncovers her nakedness, he has laid bare her flow, and she has uncovered the flow of her blood; the two of them shall be cut off from the midst of their people.
verses.20:19: And the nakedness of your mother's sister or of your father's sister you shall not uncover, for such a person has laid bare his own close relative; they shall bear their iniquity.
verses.20:20: And a man who lies with his uncle's wife has uncovered the nakedness of his uncle; they shall bear their sin, and they shall die childless.
verses.20:21: And if a man takes the wife of his brother, it is an impurity; he has uncovered the nakedness of his brother; they shall be childless.
verses.20:22: Therefore you shall observe all My statutes and all My judgments and carry them out, so that the land into which I am bringing you to live will not vomit you out.
verses.20:23: And you shall not walk in the statutes of the nation that I am casting out from before you, because they did all these things, and I loathed them.
verses.20:24: So I said to you, "You yourselves shall inherit their land, and I Myself will give it to you to possess it, a land flowing with milk and honey." I am the LORD your God, who separated you from the peoples.
verses.20:25: Therefore you must distinguish between the clean animal and the unclean, and between the unclean bird and the clean; and you must not make yourselves detestable through animal, through bird, or through anything that creeps along the ground, which I have separated for you to treat as unclean.
verses.20:26: So you shall be holy to Me, because I, the LORD, am holy, and I have separated you from the peoples to be Mine.
verses.20:27: Now a man or a woman in whom there is a spirit of the dead or a divining spirit shall surely be put to death; they shall stone them with stones; their bloodguilt is on them.'"
verses.21:1: And the LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and tell them, 'None of them shall make himself unclean for a dead person among his people,
verses.21:2: except for his blood relative who is near to him: for his mother, for his father, for his son, for his daughter, and for his brother,
verses.21:3: and for his virgin sister who is near to him, who has not belonged to a man; for her he may make himself unclean.
verses.21:4: He shall not make himself unclean as a leader among his people, so as to profane himself.
verses.21:5: They shall not make a bald spot on their heads, nor shave the edge of their beards, nor cut a gash in their flesh.
verses.21:6: They shall be holy to their God and shall not profane the name of their God, for it is the fire offerings of the LORD, the food of their God, that they present; so they must be holy.
verses.21:7: They shall not take a woman who is a prostitute or profaned, and they shall not take a woman divorced from her husband, for he is holy to his God.
verses.21:8: You shall treat him as holy, because he is the one who presents the food of your God; he shall be holy to you, for I, the LORD who sanctifies you, am holy.
verses.21:9: And if the daughter of a priest profanes herself through prostitution, it is her father whom she profanes; she shall be burned with fire.
verses.21:10: Now the priest who is the highest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been ordained to wear the garments, shall not leave his head unkempt nor tear his garments.
verses.21:11: He shall not go near any dead bodies; not for his father or for his mother shall he make himself unclean.
verses.21:12: He shall not depart from the sanctuary, nor shall he profane the sanctuary of his God, for the dedication of the anointing oil of his God is upon him. I am the LORD.
verses.21:13: And as for him, he shall take a woman in her virginity.
verses.21:14: A widow, a divorced woman, a profaned woman, a prostitute—these he shall not take; rather, he shall take a virgin from his own people as a wife,
verses.21:15: and he shall not profane his seed among his people, for I am the LORD who sanctifies him.'"
verses.21:16: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.21:17: "Speak to Aaron, saying, 'Any man from your seed throughout their generations who has a defect in him shall not approach to present the food of his God.
verses.21:18: For no man who has a defect in him shall approach: a man who is blind, or lame, or disfigured, or with an elongated limb,
verses.21:19: or a man who has a fractured foot or a fractured hand,
verses.21:20: or one who is hunchbacked, or stunted, or has a clouding in his eye, or scabies, or scabs, or a crushed testicle.
verses.21:21: No man from the seed of Aaron the priest who has a defect in him shall come near to present the fire offerings of the LORD; a defect is in him; he shall not come near to present the food of his God.
verses.21:22: He may eat the food of his God, from the most holy things and from the holy things;
verses.21:23: yet he shall not come to the curtain nor come near the altar, because a defect is in him, and he shall not profane My sanctuaries, for I am the LORD who sanctifies them.'"
verses.21:24: Thus Moses spoke to Aaron, to his sons, and to all the sons of Israel.
verses.22:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.22:2: "Speak to Aaron and to his sons that they keep themselves separate from the holy things of the sons of Israel, which they dedicate to Me, so that they do not profane My holy name. I am the LORD.
verses.22:3: Say to them, 'Throughout your generations, whichever man among all your seed approaches the holy things that the sons of Israel dedicate to the LORD while his uncleanness is on him, that person shall be cut off from before Me. I am the LORD.
verses.22:4: No man from the seed of Aaron who is leprous or has a discharge shall eat of the holy things until he is clean. And whoever touches anything unclean from a dead person, or a man from whom an emission of semen goes out,
verses.22:5: or a man who touches any swarming creature by which he becomes unclean, or a human being by whom he becomes unclean through any uncleanness of his—
verses.22:6: the person who touches such a thing shall be unclean until the evening, and he shall not eat from the holy things unless he has washed his flesh in water.
verses.22:7: Once the sun has gone down, he shall be clean, and afterward he may eat from the holy things, for it is his food.
verses.22:8: He shall not eat a carcass or anything torn, so as to become unclean by it. I am the LORD.
verses.22:9: They shall keep My charge, so that they do not bear sin on account of it and die by it when they profane it. I am the LORD who sanctifies them.
verses.22:10: No outsider shall eat anything holy; a temporary resident of a priest or a hired worker shall not eat anything holy.
verses.22:11: Yet if a priest buys a person as a purchase with his money, that one may eat of it; and those born in his house, they may eat of his food.
verses.22:12: And if the daughter of a priest marries a man who is an outsider, she herself shall not eat of the contribution of the holy things.
verses.22:13: But if the daughter of a priest becomes a widow or divorced, and has no seed, and returns to the house of her father as in her youth, she may eat from the food of her father; yet no outsider shall eat of it.
verses.22:14: And if a man eats anything holy unintentionally, he shall add a fifth part to it and give the holy thing to the priest.
verses.22:15: They shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel which they contribute to the LORD,
verses.22:16: and so cause them to bear the iniquity of guilt when they eat their holy things, for I am the LORD who sanctifies them.'"
verses.22:17: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.22:18: "Speak to Aaron, to his sons, and to all the sons of Israel, and say to them, 'Any man from the house of Israel or from the resident alien in Israel who presents his offering, for any of their vows or for any of their freewill offerings that they present to the LORD as a burnt offering,
verses.22:19: for your acceptance it must be an unblemished male among the cattle, among the sheep, or among the goats.
verses.22:20: You shall not present anything that has a defect in it, for it will not be for acceptance on your behalf.
verses.22:21: And when a man presents a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, from the herd or from the flock, it must be unblemished for acceptance; no defect shall be in it.
verses.22:22: Anything blind, or fractured, or maimed, or having a weeping sore, or scabies, or scabs—these you shall not present to the LORD, nor shall you place a fire offering from them on the altar to the LORD.
verses.22:23: As for an ox or a sheep that has an elongated or stunted limb, you may prepare it as a freewill offering, but for a vow it will not be accepted.
verses.22:24: Anything bruised, or crushed, or torn, or cut you shall not present to the LORD, nor shall you do this in your land.
verses.22:25: And from the hand of a foreigner you shall not present any of these as the food of your God, for their disfigurement is in them, a defect is in them; they shall not be accepted for you.'"
verses.22:26: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.22:27: "When an ox or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall stay seven days with its mother, and from the eighth day onward it shall be accepted as a fire-offering gift to the LORD.
verses.22:28: Yet as for an ox or a sheep, you shall not slaughter it and its young on one day.
verses.22:29: And when you sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving to the LORD, for your acceptance you shall sacrifice it.
verses.22:30: On that day it must be eaten; you shall not leave any of it over until morning. I am the LORD.
verses.22:31: You shall observe My commandments and do them. I am the LORD.
verses.22:32: And you shall not profane My holy name, and I shall be treated as holy in the midst of the sons of Israel; I am the LORD who sanctifies you,
verses.22:33: who brought you out from the land of Egypt to be God to you. I am the LORD."
verses.23:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them, 'The appointed times of the LORD, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies, these are My appointed times.
verses.23:3: For six days work may be done, but on the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, a holy assembly; you shall not do any work. It is a Sabbath to the LORD in all your dwelling places.
verses.23:4: These are the appointed times of the LORD, holy assemblies which you shall proclaim at their appointed time.
verses.23:5: In the first month, on the fourteenth of the month, between the two evenings, is Passover to the LORD.
verses.23:6: And on the fifteenth day of this month is the Feast of Unleavened Bread to the LORD; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
verses.23:7: On the first day you shall have a holy assembly; you shall not do any occupational work.
verses.23:8: And you shall present a fire offering to the LORD for seven days. On the seventh day is a holy assembly; you shall not do any occupational work.'"
verses.23:9: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:10: "Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them, 'When you enter the land that I am giving to you and reap its harvest, then you shall bring the sheaf of the first of your harvest to the priest.
verses.23:11: And he shall wave the sheaf before the LORD for your acceptance; on the day after the Sabbath the priest shall wave it.
verses.23:12: And on the day you wave the sheaf, you shall prepare an unblemished male lamb a year old for a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.23:13: And its grain offering shall be two tenth-measures of fine flour mixed with oil, a fire offering to the LORD, a soothing fragrance; and its drink offering shall be wine, a quarter of a hin.
verses.23:14: And you shall not eat bread, roasted grain, or fresh grain until this very day, until you have brought the offering of your God. It is a permanent statute throughout your generations in all your dwelling places.
verses.23:15: And you shall count for yourselves from the day after the Sabbath, from the day you bring the sheaf of the wave offering; seven complete Sabbaths they shall be.
verses.23:16: Until the day after the seventh Sabbath you shall count fifty days, and you shall present a new grain offering to the LORD.
verses.23:17: From your dwelling places you shall bring bread for a wave offering, two loaves of two tenth-measures; they shall be of fine flour; they shall be baked with leaven, as firstfruits to the LORD.
verses.23:18: And with the bread you shall present seven unblemished male lambs a year old, and one bull of the herd, and two rams. They shall be a burnt offering to the LORD, with their grain offering and their drink offerings, a fire offering, a soothing fragrance to the LORD.
verses.23:19: And you shall prepare one male goat for a sin offering, and two male lambs a year old for a sacrifice of peace offerings.
verses.23:20: And the priest shall wave them with the bread of the firstfruits as a wave offering before the LORD, with two male lambs; they shall be holy to the LORD for the priest.
verses.23:21: And you shall make a proclamation on this very day; you shall have a holy assembly. You shall not do any occupational work. It is a permanent statute in all your dwelling places throughout your generations.
verses.23:22: And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not completely reap the edge of your field when you reap, nor shall you glean the gleanings of your harvest; you shall leave them for the poor and for the resident alien. I am the LORD your God.'"
verses.23:23: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:24: "Speak to the sons of Israel, saying, 'In the seventh month, on the first of the month, you shall have a complete rest, a memorial with loud blasts, a holy assembly.
verses.23:25: You shall not do any occupational work, and you shall present a fire offering to the LORD.'"
verses.23:26: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:27: "Indeed, on the tenth of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement; you shall have a holy assembly, and you shall humble your souls and present a fire offering to the LORD.
verses.23:28: And you shall not do any work on this very day, for it is a day of atonement, to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.
verses.23:29: For every person who is not humbled on this very day shall be cut off from his kin.
verses.23:30: And as for any person who does any work on this very day, I will destroy that person from the midst of his people.
verses.23:31: You shall not do any work. It is a permanent statute throughout your generations in all your dwelling places.
verses.23:32: It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall humble your souls. On the ninth of the month at evening, from evening to evening, you shall observe your Sabbath."
verses.23:33: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:34: "Speak to the sons of Israel, saying, 'On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Feast of Booths for seven days to the LORD.
verses.23:35: On the first day is a holy assembly; you shall not do any occupational work.
verses.23:36: For seven days you shall present a fire offering to the LORD. On the eighth day you shall have a holy assembly, and you shall present a fire offering to the LORD. It is a solemn gathering; you shall not do any occupational work.
verses.23:37: These are the appointed times of the LORD, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies, for presenting a fire offering to the LORD, a burnt offering and a grain offering, a sacrifice and drink offerings, the requirement of each day on its own day,
verses.23:38: besides the Sabbaths of the LORD, and besides your gifts, and besides all your vows, and besides all your freewill offerings, which you give to the LORD.
verses.23:39: Indeed, on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you gather in the produce of the land, you shall celebrate the festival of the LORD for seven days; on the first day shall be a complete rest, and on the eighth day shall be a complete rest.
verses.23:40: And you shall take for yourselves on the first day the fruit of splendid trees, fronds of palm trees, boughs of leafy trees, and willows of the stream, and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.
verses.23:41: And you shall celebrate it as a festival to the LORD for seven days in the year. It is a permanent statute throughout your generations; in the seventh month you shall celebrate it.
verses.23:42: In booths you shall dwell for seven days; every native in Israel shall dwell in booths,
verses.23:43: so that your generations may know that I made the sons of Israel dwell in booths when I brought them out from the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.'"
verses.23:44: So Moses declared the appointed times of the LORD to the sons of Israel.
verses.24:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.24:2: "Command the sons of Israel that they bring to you pure beaten olive oil for the light, to keep a lamp lit continually.
verses.24:3: Outside the curtain of the testimony in the tent of meeting, Aaron shall arrange it from evening until morning before the LORD continually; it is a permanent statute throughout your generations.
verses.24:4: Upon the pure lampstand he shall arrange the lamps before the LORD continually.
verses.24:5: And you shall take fine flour and bake it into twelve loaves; each loaf shall be of two tenth-measures.
verses.24:6: And you shall set them in two rows, six to a row, on the pure table before the LORD.
verses.24:7: And you shall put pure frankincense on each row, that it may be a memorial portion for the bread, a fire offering to the LORD.
verses.24:8: Every Sabbath day he shall arrange it before the LORD continually; it is from the sons of Israel, an everlasting covenant.
verses.24:9: And it shall belong to Aaron and to his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place; for it is most holy to him from the fire offerings of the LORD, a permanent portion."
verses.24:10: Now the son of an Israelite woman, and he was the son of an Egyptian man, went out among the sons of Israel; and the son of the Israelite woman and an Israelite man fought in the camp.
verses.24:11: And the son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name and cursed. So they brought him to Moses. Now his mother's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
verses.24:12: And they placed him in custody, so that it might be made clear to them by the mouth of the LORD.
verses.24:13: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.24:14: "Bring the one who cursed outside the camp, and let all who heard lay their hands on his head, and let the whole congregation stone him.
verses.24:15: And to the sons of Israel you shall speak, saying, 'Any man who curses his God shall bear his sin.
verses.24:16: And the one who blasphemes the name of the LORD shall surely be put to death; the whole congregation shall surely stone him. Both the resident alien and the native, when he blasphemes the Name, shall be put to death.
verses.24:17: And if a man strikes down any human life, he shall surely be put to death.
verses.24:18: And the one who strikes down the life of an animal shall repay it, life for life.
verses.24:19: And if a man inflicts an injury on his fellow countryman, as he did, so shall it be done to him:
verses.24:20: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as he inflicts an injury on a person, so shall it be inflicted on him.
verses.24:21: And the one who strikes down an animal shall repay it, but the one who strikes down a person shall be put to death.
verses.24:22: You shall have one legal standard; it shall be for the resident alien as for the native, for I am the LORD your God.'"
verses.24:23: Then Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and they brought the one who cursed outside the camp and stoned him with stones. Thus the sons of Israel did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.25:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying,
verses.25:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them, 'When you enter the land that I am giving to you, then the land shall observe a Sabbath to the LORD.
verses.25:3: For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather its yield.
verses.25:4: But in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land, a Sabbath to the LORD; you shall not sow your field, and you shall not prune your vineyard.
verses.25:5: You shall not reap the aftergrowth of your harvest, and you shall not gather the grapes of your unpruned vine; it shall be a year of complete rest for the land.
verses.25:6: And the Sabbath of the land shall be yours for food: for you, and for your male servant and for your female servant, and for your hired worker and for your temporary resident who sojourn with you.
verses.25:7: And for your livestock and for the wild animals that are in your land, all its yield shall be for eating.
verses.25:8: And you shall count for yourself seven sabbaths of years, seven years seven times, so that the days of the seven sabbaths of years shall amount to forty-nine years for you.
verses.25:9: Then you shall sound a loud blast of the ram's horn in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month; on the Day of Atonement you shall sound the ram's horn throughout all your land.
verses.25:10: And you shall consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim release across the land for all its inhabitants. It shall be a Jubilee for you; each of you shall return to his possession, and to his clan each of you shall return.
verses.25:11: That fiftieth year shall be a Jubilee for you; you shall not sow, and you shall not reap its aftergrowth, and you shall not gather from its unpruned vines.
verses.25:12: For it is a Jubilee; it shall be holy to you. From the field you shall eat its yield.
verses.25:13: In this year of Jubilee, each of you shall return to his possession.
verses.25:14: And if you make a sale to your neighbor or buy from the hand of your neighbor, none of you shall wrong his brother.
verses.25:15: According to the number of years after the Jubilee you shall buy from your neighbor; according to the number of years of yields he shall sell to you.
verses.25:16: In proportion to the greater number of years you shall increase its purchase price, and in proportion to the smaller number of years you shall reduce its purchase price, for it is a number of yields that he is selling to you.
verses.25:17: So none of you shall wrong his neighbor, but you shall fear your God, for I am the LORD your God.
verses.25:18: Therefore you shall carry out My statutes, and keep My judgments and carry them out, so that you will dwell on the land in security.
verses.25:19: And the land will give its fruit, and you will eat to satisfaction and dwell in security on it.
verses.25:20: And if you say, "What will we eat in the seventh year? Look, we will not sow, and we will not gather our yield,"
verses.25:21: then I will command My blessing for you in the sixth year, so that it will produce the yield for the three years.
verses.25:22: And you will sow in the eighth year, and eat from the old yield; until the ninth year, until its yield comes in, you will eat the old.
verses.25:23: And the land shall not be sold irrevocably, for the land belongs to Me; for you are sojourners and temporary residents with Me.
verses.25:24: And in all the land of your possession, you shall grant redemption for the land.
verses.25:25: If your brother becomes poor and sells part of his possession, then his nearest redeemer shall come and redeem what his brother has sold.
verses.25:26: And if a man has no redeemer, yet he prospers and finds enough for its redemption,
verses.25:27: then he shall calculate the years since its sale and pay back the balance to the man to whom he sold it, and he shall return to his possession.
verses.25:28: But if he has not found enough to pay him back, then what he sold shall remain in the hand of the one who bought it until the year of Jubilee; and in the Jubilee it shall be released, and he shall return to his possession.
verses.25:29: And if a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, then its right of redemption shall remain until the end of the year of its sale; for a full year its right of redemption shall remain.
verses.25:30: But if it is not redeemed before a full year is completed for it, then the house in the city that has a wall shall stand irrevocably confirmed to the one who bought it, throughout his generations; it shall not be released in the Jubilee.
verses.25:31: The houses of the villages, however, that have no wall around them shall be reckoned with the field of the land; they shall have a right of redemption, and in the Jubilee they shall be released.
verses.25:32: As for the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities of their possession, a perpetual right of redemption shall belong to the Levites.
verses.25:33: And if one of the Levites redeems a house, then the house that was sold in the city of his possession shall be released in the Jubilee; for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the sons of Israel.
verses.25:34: But the field of the pastureland of their cities shall not be sold, for it is a perpetual possession for them.
verses.25:35: And if your brother becomes poor and his hand falters beside you, then you shall sustain him as a sojourner and a temporary resident, so that he may live with you.
verses.25:36: Do not take interest or profit from him, but fear your God, so that your brother may live with you.
verses.25:37: You shall not give him your money at interest, and for profit you shall not give your food.
verses.25:38: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan, to be God to you.
verses.25:39: And if your brother becomes poor beside you and sells himself to you, you shall not impose on him the labor of a slave.
verses.25:40: Like a hired worker, like a temporary resident he shall be with you; until the year of Jubilee he shall serve with you.
verses.25:41: Then he shall go out from you, he and his children with him, and he shall return to his clan, and to the possession of his fathers he shall return.
verses.25:42: For they are My servants, whom I brought out from the land of Egypt; they shall not be sold as a slave is sold.
verses.25:43: You shall not rule over him with harshness, but you shall fear your God.
verses.25:44: As for your male slave and your female slave whom you may have: from the nations that are around you, from them you may buy a male slave and a female slave.
verses.25:45: Moreover, from the children of the temporary residents who sojourn with you, from them you may buy, and from their clan who are with you, whom they have fathered in your land; and they shall become a possession for you.
verses.25:46: And you may leave them as an inheritance to your children after you, to inherit as a possession; forever you may make them labor. But over your brothers, the sons of Israel, none of you shall rule over his brother with harshness.
verses.25:47: And if a sojourner and temporary resident with you prospers, and your brother beside him becomes poor and sells himself to a sojourner, a temporary resident with you, or to an offshoot of a sojourner's clan,
verses.25:48: after he has sold himself, he shall have a right of redemption; one of his brothers may redeem him,
verses.25:49: or his uncle or his uncle's son may redeem him, or a close blood relative from his clan may redeem him; or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.
verses.25:50: Then he shall calculate with his buyer from the year he sold himself to him until the year of Jubilee, and the money of his sale shall correspond to the number of years; his time with him shall be like the days of a hired worker.
verses.25:51: If there are still many years, in proportion to them he shall pay back his redemption price from the money of his purchase.
verses.25:52: And if few years remain until the year of Jubilee, then he shall calculate with him; in proportion to his years he shall pay back his redemption price.
verses.25:53: Like a hired worker year by year he shall be with him; he shall not rule over him with harshness in your sight.
verses.25:54: And if he is not redeemed by these means, then he shall go out in the year of Jubilee, he and his children with him.
verses.25:55: For to Me the sons of Israel are servants; they are My servants, whom I brought out from the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.'"
verses.26:1: "You shall not make idols for yourselves, nor shall you erect a carved image or a standing pillar for yourselves, nor shall you set an engraved stone in your land to bow down upon it, for I am the LORD your God.
verses.26:2: My Sabbaths you shall observe, and My sanctuary you shall revere; I am the LORD.
verses.26:3: If you walk in My statutes and observe My commandments and carry them out,
verses.26:4: then I will give your rains in their season, and the land will yield its produce, and the trees of the field will yield their fruit.
verses.26:5: Threshing will overtake the grape harvest for you, and the grape harvest will overtake the sowing, and you will eat your bread to satisfaction and dwell securely in your land.
verses.26:6: I will give peace in the land, and you will lie down with no one to terrify you; I will eliminate vicious beasts from the land, and a sword will not pass through your land.
verses.26:7: And you will pursue your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.
verses.26:8: Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand, and your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
verses.26:9: I will turn toward you and make you fruitful and numerous, and I will uphold My covenant with you.
verses.26:10: You will eat old provisions long stored, and you will carry out the old because of the new.
verses.26:11: And I will set My dwelling place in your midst, and My soul will not loathe you.
verses.26:12: And I will walk about in your midst, and I will be God to you, and you will be a people to Me.
verses.26:13: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt so that you would not be slaves to them; and I broke the bars of your yoke and caused you to walk upright.
verses.26:14: But if you do not listen to Me and do not carry out all these commandments,
verses.26:15: and if you reject My statutes, and if your soul loathes My judgments, so that you do not carry out all My commandments and break My covenant,
verses.26:16: then I also will do this to you: I will appoint terror over you, wasting disease and burning fever that make the eyes fail and cause the soul to languish; and you will sow your seed in vain, and your enemies will eat it.
verses.26:17: And I will set My face against you, and you will be defeated before your enemies; those who hate you will dominate you, and you will flee though no one pursues you.
verses.26:18: And if even after these things you do not listen to Me, then I will discipline you further, sevenfold for your sins.
verses.26:19: I will break the pride of your might, and I will make your sky like iron and your land like bronze.
verses.26:20: Your strength will be exhausted in vain, and your land will not yield its produce, nor will the trees of the land yield their fruit.
verses.26:21: And if you walk in opposition to Me and are unwilling to listen to Me, then I will add further plagues upon you, sevenfold according to your sins.
verses.26:22: And I will unleash the wild beasts of the field against you, and they will bereave you of children, cut off your livestock, and make you few, and your roads will become desolate.
verses.26:23: And if through these things you are not disciplined by Me, but walk in opposition to Me,
verses.26:24: then I too will walk in opposition to you, and I Myself will strike you sevenfold for your sins.
verses.26:25: And I will bring upon you a sword wreaking the vengeance of the covenant; and when you gather into your cities, I will send pestilence into your midst, and you will be given into the hand of an enemy.
verses.26:26: When I break the staff of bread for you, ten women will bake your bread in one oven and bring back your bread by weight, and you will eat, yet you will not be satisfied.
verses.26:27: And if despite this you do not listen to Me, but walk in opposition to Me,
verses.26:28: then I will walk in furious opposition to you, and I too will discipline you sevenfold for your sins.
verses.26:29: And you will eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters you will eat.
verses.26:30: And I will destroy your high places and cut down your incense altars, and I will lay your corpses upon the corpses of your idols; and My soul will loathe you.
verses.26:31: And I will turn your cities into ruins and make your sanctuaries desolate, and I will not smell your soothing fragrance.
verses.26:32: And I Myself will make the land desolate, so that your enemies who dwell in it will be appalled at it.
verses.26:33: And you I will scatter among the nations, and I will unsheathe a sword after you; and your land will become a desolation, and your cities will become ruins.
verses.26:34: Then the land will make up for its Sabbaths all the days it lies desolate, while you are in the land of your enemies; then the land will rest and repay its Sabbaths.
verses.26:35: All the days it lies desolate it will keep the rest it did not keep on your Sabbaths, while you dwelt upon it.
verses.26:36: And as for those among you who remain, I will bring faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies; the sound of a driven leaf will pursue them, and they will flee as though fleeing a sword, and they will fall though no one pursues.
verses.26:37: And they will stumble over one another as if before a sword, though there is no pursuer; and you will have no ability to stand before your enemies.
verses.26:38: And you will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will devour you.
verses.26:39: And those among you who remain will waste away in their iniquity in the lands of your enemies, and also in the iniquities of their fathers they will waste away with them.
verses.26:40: Yet if they confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers, in their unfaithfulness by which they broke faith with Me, and also that they walked in opposition to Me,
verses.26:41: so that I too walked in opposition to them and brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled, and then they pay for their iniquity,
verses.26:42: then I will remember My covenant with Jacob, and also My covenant with Isaac, and also My covenant with Abraham I will remember, and the land I will remember.
verses.26:43: Yet the land will be abandoned by them and will make up for its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without them, and they themselves will pay for their iniquity, precisely because they rejected My judgments and their soul loathed My statutes.
verses.26:44: Yet even for all this, while they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them, nor will I loathe them so as to destroy them completely, breaking My covenant with them; for I am the LORD their God.
verses.26:45: But for their sake I will remember the covenant of the ancestors, whom I brought out from the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, to be God to them; I am the LORD."
verses.26:46: These are the statutes and the judgments and the laws that the LORD set between Himself and the sons of Israel at Mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.
verses.27:1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.27:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them, 'When a man makes a special vow involving the assessment of persons to the LORD,
verses.27:3: then the assessment of the male from twenty years old up to sixty years old—the assessment shall be fifty shekels of silver, by the shekel of the sanctuary.
verses.27:4: And if it is a female, then the assessment shall be thirty shekels.
verses.27:5: And if one is from five years old up to twenty years old, then the assessment of the male shall be twenty shekels, and for the female, ten shekels.
verses.27:6: And if one is from one month old up to five years old, then the assessment of the male shall be five shekels of silver, and for the female the assessment shall be three shekels of silver.
verses.27:7: And if one is from sixty years old and upward, if a male, then the assessment shall be fifteen shekels, and for the female, ten shekels.
verses.27:8: But if he is too poor for the assessment, then he shall present him before the priest, and the priest shall assess him; according to what the one making the vow can afford, the priest shall assess him.
verses.27:9: And if it is an animal from which people bring an offering to the LORD, all that he gives of it to the LORD shall be holy.
verses.27:10: He shall not replace it or exchange it, good for bad or bad for good; and if he indeed exchanges animal for animal, then both it and the one exchanged for it shall be holy.
verses.27:11: And if it is any unclean animal from which people do not bring an offering to the LORD, then he shall present the animal before the priest.
verses.27:12: And the priest shall assess it, whether good or bad; according to the assessment of the priest, so it shall be.
verses.27:13: But if he indeed redeems it, then he shall add one-fifth to the assessment.
verses.27:14: And when a man consecrates his house as holy to the LORD, then the priest shall assess it, whether good or bad; just as the priest assesses it, so it shall stand.
verses.27:15: And if the one who consecrated it redeems his house, then he shall add one-fifth of the silver of the assessment to it, and it shall be his.
verses.27:16: And if a man consecrates to the LORD part of the field of his possession, then the assessment shall be according to its seed: a homer of barley seed at fifty shekels of silver.
verses.27:17: If he consecrates his field from the year of the Jubilee, it shall stand according to the assessment.
verses.27:18: But if he consecrates his field after the Jubilee, then the priest shall calculate for him the silver according to the years that remain until the year of the Jubilee, and a deduction shall be made from the assessment.
verses.27:19: And if the one who consecrated the field indeed redeems it, then he shall add one-fifth of the silver of the assessment to it, and it shall be confirmed to him.
verses.27:20: And if he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed anymore.
verses.27:21: And the field, when it is released in the Jubilee, shall be holy to the LORD, like a devoted field; possession of it shall belong to the priest.
verses.27:22: And if he consecrates to the LORD a field he has purchased, which is not part of the field of his possession,
verses.27:23: then the priest shall calculate for him the amount of the assessment up to the year of the Jubilee, and he shall give the assessment on that day as a holy thing to the LORD.
verses.27:24: In the year of the Jubilee, the field shall return to the one from whom he purchased it, to the one to whom the possession of the land belongs.
verses.27:25: And every assessment shall be by the shekel of the sanctuary; the shekel shall be twenty gerahs.
verses.27:26: However, no one shall consecrate a firstborn among animals, which is born as firstborn to the LORD; whether ox or sheep, it belongs to the LORD.
verses.27:27: And if it is among the unclean animals, then he shall ransom it at the assessment and add one-fifth to it; and if it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold at the assessment.
verses.27:28: However, no devoted thing that a man devotes to the LORD from all that belongs to him, whether human being, animal, or part of the field of his possession, shall be sold or redeemed; every devoted thing is most holy to the LORD.
verses.27:29: No devoted one who is devoted from among humankind shall be ransomed; he shall surely be put to death.
verses.27:30: And every tithe of the land, of the seed of the land or of the fruit of the tree, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD.
verses.27:31: And if a man indeed redeems any of his tithe, he shall add one-fifth to it.
verses.27:32: And every tithe of herd and flock, everything that passes under the rod—the tenth one shall be holy to the LORD.
verses.27:33: He shall not inspect whether it is good or bad, nor shall he exchange it; and if he indeed exchanges it, then both it and the one exchanged for it shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.'"
verses.27:34: These are the commandments that the LORD commanded Moses for the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai.

notes.1:3: Hebrew li-retsono (from ratson, "favor/acceptance") means "for his acceptance," echoing the Niphal verb ve-nirtsah ("it will be accepted") in 1:4; some traditional interpreters render it "of his own free will."
notes.1:5: Hebrew zaraq ("dash/throw") denotes tossing blood in volume from a basin against the altar sides, distinct from the Hiphil hizzah ("sprinkle" drops with a finger, as in Lev 4:6).
notes.1:9: The Hiphil verb hiqtir ("turn into smoke") denotes burning a sacrifice on the altar to produce aromatic smoke, distinct from ordinary burning (saraph); ishsheh ("fire offering") stands here in the construct state before reach nichoach ("soothing fragrance," from the root nuach, "to rest/soothe").
notes.1:16: Hebrew be-notsatah carries a feminine suffix referring back to the feminine noun mur'ah ("crop"). Elsewhere notsah means "feathers/plumage" (likely the feathers on the skin over the crop), though many ancient and modern interpreters take it here as a homonym meaning "its contents."
notes.2:1: Hebrew qorban minchah is a construct phrase literally meaning "an offering of a tribute/gift"; in Leviticus, minchah specifically designates the grain offering, and nephesh ("soul/person") introduces any individual worshiper.
notes.2:2: Hebrew azkarah ("memorial portion," derived from zakar, "to remember") refers to the representative portion of the grain offering turned into smoke on the altar before the LORD. The preposition al ("along with") here carries an inclusive sense.
notes.2:6: Hebrew patot is a Qal infinitive absolute of patat ("break into bits") used with imperatival force, paired with its cognate plural noun pittim ("morsels").
notes.2:14: Hebrew aviv denotes fresh, young ears of ripening grain, and geres karmel denotes crushed kernels of newly ripened produce (karmel here means fresh garden or field grain, as in 23:14, not the mountain).
notes.3:1: Hebrew zevach shelamim is literally "a sacrifice of peace offerings" (plural shelamim, related to shalom, "peace/wholeness/well-being"), a shared sacrificial meal of fellowship and thanksgiving.
notes.3:4: Hebrew ha-yoteret al ha-kaved ("the lobe on the liver," from yatar, "to project/be left over") refers to the protruding caudate lobe of the liver; al ha-kelayot uses al in the sense "along with the kidneys."
notes.3:9: Hebrew ha-alyah temimah denotes the entire broad fat tail of Near Eastern sheep (temimah here meaning "whole/intact"), removed near ha-atseh ("the backbone" or lower spine, a term occurring only here in the Hebrew Bible).
notes.3:11: Hebrew lechem ishsheh (literally "food/bread of a fire offering") uses lechem in its broad sense of "food" to designate the altar portion allotted to the LORD (compare 3:16; 21:6; Num 28:2).
notes.4:2: The Hebrew clause literally reads 'commandments of the LORD which are not to be done' (Niphal imperfect of asah), an idiom referring specifically to negative prohibitions.
notes.4:10: Hebrew distinguishes ritual burning on the altar, using Hiphil hiqtir ('turn into smoke', as here), from burning outside the camp for disposal, using Qal and Niphal saraph ('burn', as in 4:12).
notes.4:15: The verb for slaughtering is masculine singular (Qal weqatal of shachat) with an indefinite subject ('one shall slaughter'), matching the impersonal singular usage in 4:24 and 4:33.
notes.4:22: This verse unusually opens the legal case with the relative particle asher ('when') rather than im or ki ('if'); in 4:23 and 4:28, the conjunction o ('or') introduces the sub-condition ('or if') with a Hophal perfect verb ('is made known').
notes.5:1: Literally 'voice of an adjuration' (qol alah), referring to a solemn curse or oath pronounced publicly to compel anyone with knowledge of a matter to come forward and testify.
notes.5:6: In 5:6-7 the noun asham ('guilt offering' or 'guilt penalty') designates the offering even though its sacrificial type is specified as chattat ('sin offering'), before asham denotes a distinct ram offering in 5:15-26.
notes.5:19: Hebrew pairs the Qal infinitive absolute with the Qal perfect of asham (ashom asham) for emphatic certainty, 'he has surely become guilty.'
notes.5:21: Verses 5:20-26 follow the Masoretic numbering. The rare phrase tesumet yad (literally 'a placing of the hand', occurring only here) denotes a security, pledge, or entrusted partnership.
notes.5:24: Hebrew berosho literally means 'in its head', an idiom for the full principal amount; in the next clause the Masoretic text uses the plural chamishitav ('its fifths') rather than the singular form seen in 5:16.
notes.6:2: Hebrew moqedah is a rare feminine noun from the root meaning to burn, occurring only here for the hearth or burning surface of the altar; the verb tuqad is a Hophal imperfect of the same root denoting fire kept continually burning.
notes.6:7: Hebrew haqrev is a Hiphil infinitive absolute functioning as a command with an explicit subject, the sons of Aaron.
notes.6:14: Hebrew murbekhet is a Hophal participle indicating flour thoroughly stirred or scalded with liquid, and tufine is a hapax legomenon of uncertain derivation traditionally linked to the verb meaning to bake, hence baked portions.
notes.6:20: Hebrew yizzeh is the intransitive Qal imperfect of the verb meaning to spatter, distinct from its transitive Hiphil meaning to sprinkle; the feminine suffix on aleha refers back to the spattered garment or stained part even though beged is grammatically masculine.
notes.7:18: Hebrew piggul is a rare cultic term for sacrificial flesh rendered ritually foul and unacceptable, distinct from sheqets, detestable thing, in 7:21.
notes.7:35: Hebrew mishhat, construct of mishhah, denotes an allotted or anointing portion and plays on the verb His anointing in 7:36; the subjectless third-person masculine singular Hiphil hiqriv is translated impersonally as they were presented.
notes.7:37: Hebrew milluim literally means fillings, referring to the priestly ordination rite of filling the hands and its accompanying sacrifices.
notes.8:7: The rare Qal verb vayye'pod (cognate with 'ephod') occurs only here and in Exodus 29:5, meaning to bind or secure the ephod in place with its woven band (cheshev).
notes.8:15: 'Purified' renders the privative Piel of chata' (vaychatte'), cognate with 'sin offering' (chatta't), denoting the ritual cleansing of the altar from sin or impurity; compare its denominative sense in 9:15.
notes.8:16: 'Turned into smoke' translates the Hiphil of qatar (hiqtir), used throughout Leviticus for aromatic altar offerings, in deliberate contrast to saraf ('burned with fire' in 8:17, 32; 9:11) for non-altar disposal.
notes.8:31: The Masoretic text vocalizes tsivveiti as active Piel ('I commanded'), in contrast to the passive Pual tsuvveiti ('I have been commanded') in 8:35.
notes.8:33: This verse plays three times on the root male' ('be full'): 'fulfilled' (Qal infinitive melo't), 'ordination' (millu'im, literally 'fillings'), and 'you will be ordained' (impersonal third-person Piel yemalle' et-yedkhem, literally 'one will fill your hand').
notes.9:4: The verb nir'ah is a Niphal perfect (qatal) of certainty used with 'today' to announce the imminent appearance of the LORD's glory fulfilled in 9:23.
notes.9:15: Here the Piel of chata' (vaychatte'ehu) takes the sacrificial goat as its direct object in a denominative sense, 'offered it as a sin offering,' contrasting with its privative sense ('purified' the altar) in 8:15.
notes.9:19: Verse 19 has no finite verb in Hebrew; it introduces the fat portions as a fronted topic (casus pendens) resumed as the direct object in 9:20. 'Covering fat' renders the Piel participle hamekhasseh (literally 'that which covers,' referring to the fat covering the entrails).
notes.9:22: The Masoretic text writes yadav defectively without the yod of the dual, but vocalizes it as the dual 'his hands' (contrasting with singular yado, 'his hand,' in 8:23).
notes.10:3: The Niphal imperfect verbs eqqadesh and ekkabed carry reflexive-passive force, conveying that God will be treated as holy and honored or display His holiness and glory.
notes.10:6: The Hebrew literally says do not loosen your heads, an idiom for letting the hair hang unkempt or uncovered as a mourning custom.
notes.10:18: The Hophal passive verb huva takes the direct-object marker et before its grammatical subject, its blood, and the infinitive absolute with imperfect akhol tokhelu expresses strong unfulfilled obligation.
notes.11:5: Native Masoretic order lists the rock hyrax (hashshafan, 11:5) before the hare (ha'arnevet, 11:6); both verses are retained in native Masoretic order here (some parallel verse alignments invert 11:5–6).
notes.11:13: In verses 13-19, the Hebrew noun oph covers all winged creatures, including the bat, and exact species identifications for several of the rarer birds remain uncertain.
notes.11:21: The written ketiv reads lo meaning not, whereas the read qere translated here reads lo meaning to it, yielding that have jointed legs.
notes.11:43: The verb wenitmetem is a Niphal weqatal of the root for uncleanness written defectively without the final aleph, highlighting the resulting state of defilement.
notes.12:2: Hebrew tazria (Hiphil imperfect of z-r-', literally "produces seed") is used here of a woman becoming pregnant or conceiving. The construct phrase "the impurity of her menstrual illness" translates niddat devotah (literally "the impurity/separation of her unwellness").
notes.12:4: The Masoretic Hebrew writes tohorah without a suffix ("purification") in "blood of purification" here and in v. 5 (where the preposition shifts from b- to 'al), in contrast to tohorah with a third-person feminine singular suffix ("her purification") at the end of v. 4 and in v. 6.
notes.12:6: Literally "a lamb, son of its year," a Hebrew idiom for a lamb within its first year of life. The noun chatta't ("sin offering," from the root ch-t-') here functions as a ritual purification offering rather than addressing moral transgression.
notes.12:7: The singular object suffix in vehiqrivo ("he will present it," Hiphil of q-r-b) treats the woman's offerings collectively as a single presentation. The phrase "the source of her blood" translates meqor dameiha (literally "the spring/source of her bloods," referring to postpartum bleeding).
notes.12:8: The clause "her hand does not reach enough for a sheep" translates the Hebrew idiom lo timtsa yadah dei seh, referring to insufficient financial means. The term seh denotes a single sheep or goat, referring back to the lamb in v. 6.
notes.13:2: Hebrew tsara'at (here "leprosy") encompasses a range of ritual skin, garment, and house afflictions broader than modern Hansen's disease.
notes.13:4: Hebrew literally reads "the affliction" (hannega), using abstract-for-concrete metonymy for the afflicted person; the same usage recurs in verses 12, 13, and 17.
notes.13:5: Hebrew amad be'einav literally means "stood in his eyes," indicating that the affliction appeared unchanged under the priest's observation.
notes.13:10: Hebrew michyat basar chai literally means "a reviving patch of living flesh," referring to exposed raw flesh; michyah (from chayah, "to live/revive") likewise denotes the raw regenerating area of a burn in verse 24.
notes.13:30: Hebrew neteq (from the root nataq, "to pull away/pluck") denotes a scaly scalp or beard disorder associated with hair loss, rendered "scall."
notes.13:33: Hebrew contrasts the reflexive Hithpael verb hitgallach ("shave himself") with the transitive Piel yegalleach ("shave [the scall]").
notes.13:39: Hebrew bohaq occurs only here in the Old Testament and denotes a harmless, pale skin eruption distinct from ritual leprosy.
notes.13:51: Hebrew mam'eret (Hiphil participle of ma'ar) literally means "causing pain" or "eating away," denoting an active, destructive affliction in fabric, leather, or walls (cf. 14:44).
notes.13:55: Hebrew hukkabbes is a rare Hothpaal infinitive construct ("after being washed"); the verse also reuses qarachatto and gabbachto ("its bald back or bald front," cf. vv. 42-43) metaphorically for the worn underside or topside of the fabric.
notes.14:3: Hebrew tsara'at, rendered "leprosy" here, covers a range of ritually defiling skin disorders as well as discoloring or moldlike conditions on garments and plastered walls (vv. 34, 55), not solely modern Hansen's disease. "Healed in the leprous person" translates a pregnant Hebrew construction (literally "healed from the leprous person," i.e., healed away from him), using the Qal passive participle tsaru'a alongside the Pual participle metsora' in v. 2.
notes.14:10: Hebrew issaron ("tenth-measure") is one-tenth of an ephah (a dry measure of roughly 2.2 liters), and a log is a small liquid measure equal to one-twelfth of a hin (roughly one-third of a liter).
notes.14:21: "His means are insufficient" renders the Hebrew idiom 'en yado masseget (literally "his hand does not reach," Hiphil participle of nasag), which recurs in vv. 22, 30, 31, and 32 to express financial ability.
notes.14:37: "Sunken patches" translates the hapax legomenon sheqa'arurot (apparently from shaqa', "to sink"), and "lower than the wall" renders shaphal min-haqqir, meaning recessed beneath the wall surface.
notes.14:49: "To purify" renders the privative Piel infinitive lechatte' (from chata', "to sin," here meaning "to purge from defilement," also in v. 52), distinct from the Piel of taher ("to cleanse" or "declare clean," vv. 7, 11, 48).
notes.15:2: Hebrew basar ("flesh") is used here and in vv. 3 and 19 as a euphemism for the genital organ.
notes.15:3: Hebrew rar (Qal perfect of the hapax legomenon verb rir, "ooze" or "run") and hechtim (Hiphil perfect of chatam, "seal up" or "obstruct") cover both a continuous discharge and a blocked one.
notes.15:13: Hebrew mayim chayyim ("living water") is the standard idiom for fresh, flowing water from a spring or stream.
notes.15:23: The masculine pronoun hu ("it") has no explicit antecedent and is widely understood to refer to any object lying on the bed or article on which the menstruating woman sits.
notes.15:31: The verb vehizzartem is the Hiphil of nazar ("set apart" or "keep separate"); some ancient versions reflect a form of zahar ("warn").
notes.16:2: Hebrew hakkapporet ("atonement cover") is derived from the root kafar ("cover" or "atone").
notes.16:8: The meaning of Hebrew Azazel is uncertain; it has been understood variously as a wilderness figure or demon, a remote rugged place, or a term signifying complete removal ("the goat that departs").
notes.16:21: Hebrew ish itti uses the hapax legomenon adjective itti (from et, "time"), meaning a man ready or designated for the occasion. In addition, yadav ("his hands") is written defectively without yod in the Masoretic Text.
notes.16:22: Hebrew erets gezerah (from gazar, "cut off") literally means "a cut-off land," denoting an isolated, uninhabited region.
notes.16:32: Literally "whose hand one fills," using the Hebrew idiom mille yad ("fill the hand") for priestly ordination; both yimshach ("anoint") and yemalle ("fill") are indefinite third-person singular active verbs rendered passively.
notes.17:7: Hebrew se'irim (plural of sa'ir, literally "hairy ones" or "he-goats") refers to goat-shaped desert demons or deities (cf. 2 Chr 11:15; Isa 13:21).
notes.17:9: Hebrew me'ammayw uses the plural noun ("from his kinspeople"), contrasting with the singular noun in "from the midst of his people" in vv. 4 and 10.
notes.17:11: The Hebrew noun nephesh ("life" or "person") occurs three times in this verse, linking the life of flesh in blood to human lives; the preposition be- in bannephesh ("by means of the life") is instrumental or denotes equivalence.
notes.17:14: Literally, "its blood is in/as its life" (damo venaphsho hu'), an emphatic Hebrew construction combining casus pendens with a beth of equivalence or identity.
notes.18:6: The Hebrew pairs the distributive singular phrase "any man ... his flesh" with the second-person plural verb lo' tiqrevu ("you shall not approach"); she'er besaro is literally "flesh of his flesh," an idiom for close blood kin.
notes.18:18: The Qal infinitive construct litsror derives from tsarar ("to be a rival wife" or "to create rivalry," cognate with tsarah, "rival wife," in 1 Sam 1:6).
notes.18:20: Literally, "you must not give your lying for seed" (lo'-titten shekhavtekha lezara'), an idiom for sexual intercourse; the noun zera' ("seed") also creates a verbal link to "your seed" (mizzar'akha) in v. 21.
notes.18:21: The Hiphil infinitive construct leha'avir (literally "to cause to pass over") appears here without the phrase "through the fire" found in parallel texts (e.g., Deut 18:10; 2 Kgs 23:10), denoting dedication or child sacrifice to Molech.
notes.18:30: Hebrew uses the same noun huqqot ("statutes") for the nations' "abominable statutes" (cf. v. 3) as for the LORD's "statutes" in vv. 4, 5, and 26, underscoring the deliberate contrast between them.
notes.19:5: Hebrew lirsonkem literally means "for your acceptance," referring to cultic acceptability before the LORD (matching the Niphal verb yeraseh, "it will be accepted," in v. 7) rather than mere personal inclination.
notes.19:16: Hebrew al-dam re'eka literally means "upon/against the blood of your neighbor," an idiom understood either as taking a stand against a neighbor's life (for instance, through false accusation) or as standing idly by while a neighbor's life is in mortal danger.
notes.19:19: The rare Hebrew noun sha'atnez (occurring only here and in Deut 22:11) denotes cloth of mixed weave, explained in Deut 22:11 specifically as wool and linen woven together.
notes.19:20: Hebrew biqqoret is a hapax legomenon from the root bqr ("inquire/examine"), denoting a judicial inquiry or assessment, though interpreters have also understood it as a penalty, scourging, or indemnity. Note also the emphatic construction hofdeh lo nifdatah, pairing a Hophal infinitive absolute with a Niphal perfect ("not at all been redeemed").
notes.19:23: Hebrew va'araltem orlato et-piryo literally says "you shall treat as uncircumcised its foreskin, namely its fruit," applying the metaphor of uncircumcision to forbid eating a fruit tree's produce during its first three years.
notes.20:3: Hebrew zera ("seed") here denotes a person's children/offspring (retaining the verbal link with Lev 18:20–21; cf. 20:2, 4).
notes.20:9: Hebrew damav (literally "his bloods," plural) is a standard legal idiom for bloodguilt, here meaning the offender bears sole responsibility for his own execution. The conjunction ve- ("and") in "his father and his mother" carries the legal disjunctive sense "or" (as also in v. 19).
notes.20:17: Hebrew hesed here is a rare homonym (hesed II, cf. Prov 14:34) meaning "disgrace" or "reproach," distinct from the common word hesed ("loyal love, kindness").
notes.20:25: The Piel infinitive letamme carries a declarative or estimative sense ("to treat/declare as unclean"), while the verse arranges the pairs chiastically: clean-to-unclean for animals, then unclean-to-clean for birds.
notes.20:27: Hebrew ki-yihyeh bahem ov o yidde'oni literally means "when there is in them a spirit of the dead or a divining ('knowing') spirit." By metonymy, the same two nouns denote the mediums and spirit-diviners who consult such spirits in 19:31 and 20:6.
notes.21:4: Hebrew ba'al be'ammav is syntactically difficult and may mean 'as a leader among his people' or 'as a husband among his people' (referring to a wife or relatives by marriage). The form lehehallo is a Niphal infinitive construct of halal ('profane') with a 3ms suffix, 'so as to profane himself.'
notes.21:5: The ketiv is written yqrhh; the qere yiqrechu ('they shall make bald'), translated here, is plural like the following verbs and is followed by the cognate noun qorhah ('a bald spot').
notes.21:9: The verb tehel is Niphal imperfect 3fs of halal I ('profane herself'), echoing the Piel participle mehallelet ('she profanes') in the following clause.
notes.21:10: Literally 'and one has filled his hand' (Piel perfect of male' with an impersonal subject), the standard priestly idiom for ordination.
notes.21:20: Several rare defect terms in vv. 18-20 have uncertain exact meanings: harum (v. 18) likely denotes a cleft or flattened nose or face, saru'a (v. 18) an abnormally long limb, daq (v. 20) someone stunted or a dwarf, and teballul (v. 20) a blurring or spot in the eye.
notes.22:2: The Niphal yinnazeru (from nazar) means 'keep themselves separate' or 'abstain.' In the Masoretic clause order, the relative clause 'which they dedicate to Me' follows 'My holy name,' resuming 'the holy things of the sons of Israel.'
notes.22:16: The Hiphil weqatal vehissi'u (from nasa', 'cause to bear') has an ambiguous object pronoun 'otam ('them'), referring either to the Israelites (whom negligent priests cause to incur guilt) or reflexively to the offenders themselves; 'avon 'ashmah is a construct chain, literally 'iniquity of guilt.'
notes.22:19: Hebrew lirtsonekhem ('for your acceptance,' also in v. 29) indicates that the offering must meet the standard to be accepted on the worshiper's behalf, matching leratson ('for acceptance') in vv. 20-21 and the Niphal of ratsah ('be accepted') in vv. 23, 25, and 27.
notes.22:24: The four Qal passive participles (ma'uk, katut, natuq, karut) refer to methods of animal castration or testicular injury; the closing clause ('nor shall you do this in your land') is commonly understood to forbid castrating animals in Israel.
notes.23:5: Hebrew beyn ha-arbayim (dual of erev) literally means "between the two evenings," an idiom referring either to twilight between sunset and dusk or to the late afternoon hours before sunset.
notes.23:7: Hebrew meleket avodah literally means "work of labor/service," denoting regular occupational work, in contrast to the total prohibition of all melakah ("work") on the Sabbath (v. 3) and the Day of Atonement (vv. 28-31).
notes.23:11: Hebrew mimmohorat ha-shabbat ("on the day after the Sabbath") has been interpreted either as the day after the first festival day of Unleavened Bread or as the day after the weekly Sabbath falling during the festival; similarly, "seven complete Sabbaths" in v. 15 denotes seven full weeks culminating in the seventh Sabbath (v. 16).
